title: Task Aware Modulation using Representation Learning: An Approach for Few Shot Learning in Environmental Systems
ml_methods: TAM-RL (Task Aware Modulation using Representation Learning)
testbed_rationale: The study targets few-shot regional streamflow and point-scale carbon flux time series prediction rather than numerical climate/weather model subgrid parameterization testbeds.
pain_points: Entity characteristics (e.g., soil, vegetation, geology) are often unavailable or highly uncertain for sparsely observed entities.
Equifinality in traditional process-based model calibration when applied to sparsely observed entities.
Standard gradient-based meta-learning methods (e.g., MAML) suffer from high computational and memory training costs and struggle on multimodal/heterogeneous task distributions.
Current framework cannot handle missing driver or response data observations.
extraction_notes: Research funded by NSF LEAP Science and Technology Center (award 2019625). Evaluates an amortized meta-learning architecture (TAM-RL) combining an inverse BiLSTM representation network, MLP FiLM modulation, and forward LSTM predictor.
